comments.note: tests/bootstrap.php defines TESTS_ROOT using the `const` keyword at file scope (line 21: `const TESTS_ROOT = __DIR__;`). The seeding script uses `define('TESTS_ROOT', ...)` before requiring bootstrap.php, which means bootstrap.php's `const TESTS_ROOT` will generate a PHP E_WARNING ('Constant TESTS_ROOT already defined') on every `composer seed-tests` invocation. The first definition (from the script) wins, so the value is correct, but the warning is noise. The fix would be to update tests/bootstrap.php to guard the constant with `if (!defined('TESTS_ROOT')) { define('TESTS_ROOT', __DIR__); }` — this change is out of scope for WP-003 but should be addressed in a follow-up.

The seeding script does not wrap the TestSuiteBootstrap::seedSystemUsers() call in a try/catch. If seeding fails, PHP will output the unhandled exception with a raw stack trace. Adding a try/catch around the call (and echoing a user-friendly error message followed by exit(1)) would make the CLI experience cleaner and allow CI pipelines to detect failure reliably via exit code.

comments.note: tests/bootstrap.php line 21 uses `const TESTS_ROOT = __DIR__` unconditionally. When seed-test-db.php runs `define('TESTS_ROOT', __DIR__)` first and then requires bootstrap.php, PHP emits E_WARNING 'Constant TESTS_ROOT already defined'. The value is correct (both resolve to the tests/ directory) but the warning is noise in CLI output and could mask real warnings in CI. Fix: change bootstrap.php to use `defined('TESTS_ROOT') || define('TESTS_ROOT', __DIR__)` or a `!defined` guard. Out of scope for WP-003; recommend a follow-up task.

seed-test-db.php does not wrap TestSuiteBootstrap::seedSystemUsers() in try/catch. A failure will produce a raw PHP stack trace. Adding try/catch with exit(1) would improve CI reliability and user-facing output. The method itself does handle DB rollback internally, so data integrity is not at risk — this is purely a DX/UX improvement.

Both scenarios are handleable and do not represent implementation defects.
